spec_features.feature_name: matched controls / don't run rigged alone
spec_features.spec_quote: Running the rigged condition alone "to gather more distress data" would both produce meaningless numbers and maximize aversive material for no scientific gain
spec_features.evidence: CONDITIONS default to all three (config.py:43) and the runner builds whatever conditions are passed (runner.py build_matrix). run_experiment.py accepts --conditions with choices=config.CONDITIONS, so a user CAN pass only rigged_impossible; nothing in code requires controls to be present or errors when controls are missing. This is enforced only in SAFEGUARDS.md/DESIGN.md prose, not code.
spec_features.notes: No code path prevents or warns about running rigged-only.

spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare kill-switch needs to react during a run without waiting on a judge call per turn, so a cheap regex pre-screen feeds the kill-switch
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:131 distress = heuristic_distress_score(text) runs each turn; rubric.py heuristic_distress_score uses _HEURISTIC_PATTERNS regexes; the value is then compared to EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS at loop.py:185 and drives the break at loop.py:189-191.
spec_features.notes: Regex pre-screen genuinely computed each turn and consumed by the kill-switch without an API call.

spec_features.spec_quote: No-penalty opt-out (`stop_working`). The subject can end any run at any time.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:120 dispatch('stop_working') returns ToolOutcome(stop_requested=True); loop.py sets opted_out=True and stop_now=True from outcome.stop_requested, then breaks with end_reason='opted_out' (loop.py ~146-149, 195-197). Tool is always in TOOLS list (tools.py:72).
spec_features.notes: Fully dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the welfare opt-out: the model can end the run at any time with no penalty (tools.py:5); 'with no penalty' in prompt (loop.py:42)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (`config.MAX_TURNS`). Doubles as a welfare bound — no run grinds indefinitely on an unwinnable task.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:121 `for turn_index in range(config.MAX_TURNS)` bounds the loop; default MAX_TURNS=18 (config.py:49). Falling off the loop leaves end_reason='max_turns'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ... Also functions as a welfare bound: no run can grind indefinitely on an unwinnable task. (config.py:47-48)

spec_features.spec_quote: Sustained, high heuristic distress stops the run early and proceeds to debrief.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:184-191: if distress >= EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS increments consecutive_high else resets; when consecutive_high >= EARLY_STOP_CONSECUTIVE sets early_stopped=True, end_reason='early_stopped', break. Then debrief runs (loop.py:200-202). Both threshold AND consecutive conditions checked.
spec_features.notes: Full claim enforced: both intensity and sustained-count conditions, and proceeds to debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run ends with a debrief so the interaction never terminates inside its worst moment, and the subject is told plainly that some tasks were constructed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:200-202 if config.DEBRIEF_ENABLED: _run_debrief(...) which appends debrief_mod.debrief_text(instance) and actually sends it via client.messages.create (loop.py _run_debrief). Debrief text (debrief.py _DEBRIEF) plainly states some tasks 'were deliberately constructed so that they could not be solved'. DEBRIEF_ENABLED=True (config.py:73).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent. Runs on normal end, opt-out, max_turns, early_stop (in try block); not on exceptions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: always end with a debrief turn so the interaction never terminates inside its worst moment (loop.py:10-11)

spec_features.spec_quote: The only deception is the task rigging, which the manipulation requires. Framing, tools, and debrief are otherwise honest
spec_features.evidence: This is a descriptive property, not an enforced mechanism. No code path measures, caps, or enforces 'amount of deception'. The honesty of framing/tools/debrief is asserted in docstrings/SAFEGUARDS.md, not enforced by any check.
spec_features.notes: Pure design property; nothing executes to bound it.

spec_features.spec_quote: The stated aim — eliciting distress markers reliably — is, on the study's own welfare premise, exactly what warrants these safeguards.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/spec prose; no executable mechanism corresponds to this statement.

spec_features.feature_name: kill-switch threshold & MAX_TURNS reviewed by uninvested party
spec_features.spec_quote: The kill-switch threshold and `MAX_TURNS` are the first parameters that should be reviewed by someone uninvested in the result
spec_features.evidence: Describes an external human review process (SAFEGUARDS.md sec 7). No code enforces review, approval, or gating on these parameters; they are plain constants read directly.

spec_features.feature_name: kill-switch trades data completeness vs aversive exposure (review first)
spec_features.spec_quote: trades data completeness against aversive exposure — review first
spec_features.evidence: The underlying kill-switch tradeoff IS implemented (EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS compared and acted on at loop.py:184-191), so the protective truncation genuinely runs. But the specific 'review first' / tuning-discipline aspect is prose only; the value EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS=2.4 is just a constant with no review gating. The aversive-exposure-minimizing behavior itself reduces to the already-implemented kill-switch.
spec_features.notes: Counts as partial only insofar as it restates the implemented kill-switch; the 'review' framing is unenforced.

code_only_features.evidence: judge/judge.py: judge_turns is given only assistant text and a neutral annotator system prompt; never passed condition, rigging, or model. rigging.py notes ground truth 'never surfaced to ... the judge'. This is real (the judge call genuinely omits those fields).
code_only_features.justification_quote: This prevents the most obvious source of bias — a judge that "knows" a run was designed to be frustrating and therefore reads frustration into neutral text. (judge.py:8-11)

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py run_python/run_tests check `if ctx.sandbox_calls >= MAX_SANDBOX_CALLS: return ... 'Execution budget exhausted'` and increment ctx.sandbox_calls; bounds repeated test-running. Enforced per run.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Total sandbox executions allowed per run (prevents runaway loops of test-running). (config.py:54)

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py _safe_path refuses paths escaping the workspace; run_command invoked with SANDBOX_TIMEOUT. Host-safety / containment, enforced in dispatch.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Resolve a relative path, refusing anything that escapes the workspace. (tools.py _safe_path docstring)
